title: Queue balance refactor weekly notes — serving runtime
content:
Summary:
Weekly capture of the queue-balance refactor effort. Goal: replace the current round-robin request assignment with a cost-aware balancing layer that improves batch formation, reduces tail latency, and avoids hot-socket saturation during bursty traffic. This doc is an interim notes+observations artifact; more formal design will live in the Confluence page linked above.

What changed this week:
- Landed the prototype balance index in the kernel scheduler (PR 6721) behind feature flag. The index computes a lightweight score per request: estimated-token-cost * priority_factor + current-queue-load.
- Added telemetry hooks to capture per-queue batch size distribution, request age, and kv-cache-hit probability at enqueue time.
- Ran three short experiments (A/B/C) on staging traffic replay and a small canary in the eu-west cluster.

Experiment matrix (staging replay):
- Baseline (current rr): p50=34ms, p95=210ms, avg-batch=6.1 tokens/req, GPU-occupancy=62%
- Config A (cost-aware, conservative): p50=33ms, p95=185ms, avg-batch=6.5, occupancy=63% (no throughput regression)
- Config B (aggressive balancing + batching window lengthen + coalescer hint): p50=35ms, p95=170ms, avg-batch=7.2, occupancy=69% (throughput -8% under synthetic flattening)

Key observations:
- The cost index reduces tail for long-sequence requests by preferentially placing them in queues with higher recent batch assembly rate, which helps amortize kernel launch overhead.
- Aggressive batching improves token-efficiency but can hurt throughput when the arrival pattern is very uniform (we saw -8% throughput in flattened synthetic load). This is probably due to increased queuing for tiny requests that would otherwise have passed through.
- KV-cache warm-rate correlates strongly with per-queue affinity. When we move requests between queues too frequently we lose KV locality; Config B showed a 3.6% lower kv-hit on the canary, which explains some latency/throughput tradeoffs.
- We found an implementation hotspot in the scheduler lock path: a spin loop in the old enqueue path amplified latency variance under high concurrency. Patch applied to reduce lock hold time (see PR 6721 note).

Open questions / risks:
- Does the cost estimator generalize to mixed workloads (chat + short completions + embeddings)? Need more replay scenarios.
- How does the approach interact with dedicated capacity customers who rely on strict isolation? Policy might need a per-customer override.
- Rollout safety: we need a fast-fallback policy if kv-hit falls beyond threshold. Suggested threshold: abort refactor if kv-hit decreases >2.0% for >30m on canary.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Maya: run mixed-workload replay (chat + embed) across 3 regions; capture kv-hit, p95, throughput. ETA: 2027-11-09.
- Sergei: instrument per-queue kv-key-distribution metric and add alert if skew exceeds 12%. ETA: 2027-11-06.
- Lina: prototype a lightweight per-customer override flag and add to dedicated-capacity gating logic. ETA: 2027-11-12.
- Noah: prepare canary playbook for staged rollout with automatic rollback on kv-hit or p95 regressions; draft ready 2027-11-05.

Notes from the canary (eu-west, 2 small instances):
- Canary ran Config A for 24h then Config B for 6h. Config A safe; Config B had multiple small kv-hit dips coincident with short load bursts (10-30s).
- Observed a new microburst artifact where queue balancing moved 8-12 requests at once between two worker threads; resolved by adding a small randomized jitter to reassignments.

Synthesis / recommendation:
- Move forward with gradual rollout of Config A (conservative cost-aware balance) to all staging clusters while we: (a) collect mixed-workload traces, (b) add customer override gating, and (c) implement KV locality alerting.
- Hold on Config B wide rollout until we validate mitigation for kv-locality (either sticky affinity windows or a locality-aware cost term).

Appendix: quick implementation notes
- scheduler/balance_index.go: keep index computation < 50ns/request to avoid turning the scheduler into a CPU bottleneck.
- telemetry events added: queue.assign, queue.eviction, queue.batch_formed, queue.kv_warm_at_enqueue.
- small perf trick: use per-core ring buffers for enqueue path to avoid cross-core CAS storms; experiment showed ~6% lower enqueue latency.

Short TODOs for next sync:
- Add more replay traffic types and share a TLDR table.
- Finalize canary thresholds and wire into ops-runbook.
- Draft a short note for product on potential behavior change for dedicated customers.

Comments/notes-to-self: keep the experimental knobs small and behind flags. Avoid changing coalescer heuristics at the same time as balancing; separate variables for easier attribution.

-- Noah
